title: Executors, futures, and virtual threads — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: A service makes several independent blocking lookups. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does Future.get(timeout, unit) time out?

options.text: The caller’s wait for a result

questions.explanation: The task may continue unless cancelled or otherwise bounded.

questions.prompt: Who should close a task executor?

options.text: The garbage collector on a schedule

questions.explanation: Explicit ownership prevents leaked work and resources.

questions.prompt: Should virtual threads usually be pooled to reuse a fixed set of them?
questions.explanation: Use one virtual thread per task and bound scarce resources separately.

questions.prompt: Does cancel(true) guarantee an immediate task stop?
Why can a fixed worker pool still run out of memory?

options.text: An unbounded queue can accumulate pending tasks
Every fixed pool starts infinite workers

questions.explanation: Worker limits do not imply queue or admission limits.

questions.prompt: Does the sample’s output reveal which task finished first?
questions.explanation: The caller explicitly combines results in a chosen order.

Two tasks receive independent virtual threads; execution order is unspecified. get waits as needed; output order is determined by concatenation, not task completion order. The executor closes after its tasks finish.
